# sitegen

Builds `content/` into a small browsable site under `out/`: an index listing the
posts, an about page, and one page per post, sharing navigation and a stylesheet.

## Quick start

    python3 build.py        # build the site into out/
    python3 serve.py        # serve at http://localhost:8000

## Writing a post

1. Create a new file in `content/posts/` with a `.md` extension.
2. Add a front-matter header with `title` and `date`:

   ```
   ---
   title: My post title
   date: 2026-09-18
   ---

   # My post title

   Your text here. **Bold** and [links](https://example.com) work.
   ```

3. Run `python3 build.py` (or `make build`).
4. Open `out/posts/my-post-title.html` in a browser, or run `python3 serve.py`
   and visit `http://localhost:8000/posts/my-post-title.html`.

The post appears on the home page automatically, sorted by date (newest first).

## Markdown subset

Headings (`#`, `##`, `###`), paragraphs, `**bold**`, and `[text](url)` links.
That is all.

## Pages

Top-level pages (like `about.md`) live directly in `content/`. Posts live in
`content/posts/`. Both are built the same way; only posts appear in the index
listing.

## Tests

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Serve the built site at http://localhost:8000."""

import http.server
import socketserver
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).parent
OUT = ROOT / "out"
PORT = 8000


def main():
    if not OUT.exists():
        print("out/ does not exist. Run: python3 build.py")
        raise SystemExit(1)

    import functools
    handler = functools.partial(
        http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler, directory=str(OUT)
    )
    with socketserver.TCPServer(("", PORT), handler) as httpd:
        print(f"Serving {OUT} at http://localhost:{PORT}")
        httpd.serve_forever()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

.PHONY: build serve test

build:
	python3 build.py

serve:
	python3 serve.py

test:
	python3 -m unittest discover -s tests

write your own text. **Bold** and [links](https://example.com) work.

Delete this file when you have written your first real post.
